evidence: Judged the DRAFT ('especially if it has to do with trauma or memories. The mind makes it symbolic, squashes things together, distorts, dramatizes, pulls from cultural influences, fears etc. So take it as an image and get some outside help!') against SOURCE ('especially if it relates to trauma and memory. [same middle sentence] So, treat it like an image and get some help outside of yourself!') and inside CONTEXT, where it is the closing REMEMBER note of 'Capacity before content' and occurs once, word for word. DOES WHAT THE_CHANGE SAYS: the first sentence's ending and the last sentence are the quoted Emulate words; the middle sentence is identical to the source (compared word by word). MEANING: 'relates to' to 'has to do with', 'treat it like' to 'take it as' and 'help outside of yourself' to 'outside help' are plain equivalents. The one real shift is 'trauma and memory' to 'trauma or memories', which widens the 'especially' trigger from the pair to either; it fits the guide's own 'symbolic information or a hypothesis, never proof of history', adds no claim, and I judge it immaterial. No new fact, name, number or first-person claim (C03, C04 absent). READS RIGHT: 'it' is the hypnotic imagery of the first clause, as in the approved paragraph, and 'take it as an image' echoes 'imagery' so the last 'it' is anchored (C02 absent); 'So' follows from the middle sentence (the mind distorts it, so treat it as an image); 'memories' picks up the memory in the script paragraph just above it. TELL ROWS: checked T01 to T29 and C01 to C04 on the literal paragraph; none is actually happening, so resolved_tell_ids is empty. Looked at hardest: T29 (the last sentence is a 'So...' conclusion, but without it the paragraph never tells the reader what to do and 'get some outside help' is a new consideration, so not the tell); T15 (this is a reword, but the swaps go to plainer, more probable words, not rarer ones, and the structure is the approved one); T13 and T09 (the claim, the open list ending 'etc.' and the instruction each carry something specific; a three-sentence reminder in the approved order is not slot-filling, and the change adds none); T12 and T21 (the six-item sentence is one job and an open list, not a closed taxonomy); T20 and T28 (the closer is a plain instruction, not an aphorism or uplift, and it opens a new point rather than recapping the section). LINTER: B4/E15 flags the unchanged middle sentence, the author's approved open enumeration with one job: accepted. D9 is expected for a local rewording of an approved paragraph that keeps its order; T13 and T09 checked above: accepted. O45 flags 'So take it as an image and get some outside help!': it is the paragraph's own closing caution, approved in batch 470 and part of the meaning to keep, so dropping it would break 'keeps the meaning'; the draft rewords it in place and adds or repeats no safety line, and it does change what the reader does here (read imagery about memory as an image, not as history, and seek outside help with it), a different job from the section's earlier 'getting support' when flooded: accepted. Caveat for the author, not a defect of the rewording: like the source, the line is phrased as an unconditional instruction (the 'sometimes-true point said as a rule' test), so whether to keep that approved caution at all is a separate decision from this change.
